title: Marketplace plugin check: detect opum-lore in lore init and lore agents --check (claude + codex), four states, LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS=off
description: Routed by opum-agent OPAG-421. Binding record: opum-doc main 7831fff, docs/adr/distribute-lore-and-quest-agent-skills-through-the-plugin-marketplace.md (Amendments 1-4), rulings (a), (d), 18, 20, 22, 23, 24, 26. Parity with quest-cli QCLI-371 (opum-ai/quest-cli#266, merged 30a6846) under ruling (d): read its implementation by ref and match it. DETECT only through the agent CLI's public list command, never its internal files: 'claude plugin list --json' (rows id/enabled/version/scope/projectPath) and 'codex plugin list --json' (.installed[] rows pluginId/enabled/version), matching id opum-lore@opum. STATES, machine-readable kebab-case: installed, disabled (enabled:false, never reported as installed), not-installed, not-detectable (binary missing, non-zero exit, unparseable output). CLAUDE SCOPE (ruling 26): drop local/project rows whose projectPath is not this project (realpath or a prefix), the most specific applicable row decides (local > project > user > managed > synced), and report scope. INIT: for each selected claude or codex target, after target selection and before any skill write, report data.plugins.<runtime> = {runtime, id, state, version?, scope?, reason?, remedy?}; no mutation, no exit-code change. CHECK (lore agents --check): data.plugin, same shape, for the target runtime; no mutation. REMEDIES: install = '<cli> plugin marketplace add opum-ai/opum-marketplace && <install>'; enable = 'claude plugin enable <id>' (Codex names the config.toml key). OFF SWITCH (ruling 23): LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS=off makes every runtime not-detectable and spawns no claude/codex process; the test suite sets it by default (bunfig preload or equivalent) so no test touches the developer's real install.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Detection covers claude and codex through their public list commands only, producing the four ruling-24 states, with ruling-26 scope handling on the Claude side, proven by tests over recorded list outputs including a foreign-project row and a disabled row

lore init reports data.plugins.<runtime> for each selected claude/codex target before any skill write, and lore agents --check reports data.plugin, with no mutation and no exit-code change, field names matching QCLI-371
LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS=off yields not-detectable and spawns no runtime process, and the test suite runs with it set by default
Parity cited: the implementing commit SHA is sent to quest-cli for QCLI-371 AC4

plan: 1. src/core/agent-plugins.ts: pure state model (four ruling-24 states), remedies and detection over a listing, field names and remedy strings from QCLI-371 at 30a6846 with opum-lore@opum; port types declared here so core imports no adapter.

2. src/adapters/agent-plugins.ts: CliAgentPluginPort (claude/codex plugin list --json only, hard SIGKILL deadline, ruling-26 scope precedence local>project>user>managed>synced, foreign projectPath rows dropped), DisabledAgentPluginPort, createAgentPluginPort honouring LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS=off. The disabled port answers synchronously so the off path keeps runAgents/runInit synchronous.

3. Wire lore init (flag path and wizard): data.plugins.<runtime> for each selected claude/codex target, detected before any bridge write. Wire lore agents --check: data.plugin for the armed runtime. No mutation, no exit-code change. Injectable agentPlugins seam through RunContext.
4. bunfig.toml preload sets LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS=off; package.json test scripts set it at the process boundary too (measured: Bun children do not inherit a preload process.env mutation).

5. Tests over recorded list outputs (foreign-project row, disabled row, scope precedence, unreadable shape, missing binary, non-zero exit), off-switch-spawns-nothing with a positive control, mutation check on one state mapping.
6. Docs: cli-surface agents/init, cli-contract kind table, lore instructions text if it describes these outputs. Gates: full bun test and bun run lore check.
implementationNotes: IMPLEMENTED on branch lcli-592-plugin-detection. Parity read by ref via the GitHub API (git -C into sibling checkouts is refused by the worktree-isolation guard): quest-cli 30a6846 src/adapters/agents/cli-agent-plugins.ts, src/application/agents/agent-plugins.ts, src/ports/agent-plugins.ts and both qcli371 tests; opum-doc 7831fff ADR. Field names {runtime,id,state,version?,scope?,reason?,remedy?}, the four state strings, remedy strings and the five-level Claude scope precedence match QCLI-371 with the id swapped to opum-lore@opum. New: src/core/agent-plugins.ts (pure; no spawn), src/adapters/agent-plugins.ts (claude/codex plugin list --json only, SIGKILL deadline, LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS=off port answers synchronously so the off path keeps runAgents/runInit synchronous). Wired: lore init data.plugins.<runtime> (flag path and wizard, detected before any bridge write; wizard reads it before the first byte of the run); lore agents --check data.plugin plus data.plugins. No exit-code change, no mutation.

MEASURED 2026-09-26, lore from source at this branch, bun 1.3.14. (1) Real list shapes recorded read-only from claude 2.1.283 and codex-cli 0.155.1; fixtures in test/agent-plugins.test.ts keep every emitted key, home redacted. (2) Bun children do NOT inherit a preload's process.env mutation (Bun.spawn, Bun.spawnSync and node execFileSync all printed unset), so the bunfig preload protects in-process runs only; no test in test/ spawns lore for init or agents, and the new subprocess cases pass LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS in the child env explicitly. package.json not changed: CI runs bun test directly, so a script-level env would not reach CI. (3) Live read-only end-to-end: lore agents --check in this repo reported claude installed 0.9.0 scope user, exit 0; a scratch init --claude --codex reported codex not-installed. (4) Gates: full bun test exit 0 (3519 pass, 0 fail, 3520 ran, 110 files); bun run lore check exit 0 (82 files, 0 errors); tsc 0; biome 0. (5) Mutation: checkFromListing's enabled:false branch mapped to installed. Predicted 12 red (every case asserting disabled), observed exactly those 12 red, 219 green including the foreign-row-does-not-mask case; reverted.

DESIGN QUESTIONS for the orchestrator (implemented a reading, not decided): (A) lore agents has no --target and checks the Claude and Codex bridges in one call where both exist, so a single data.plugin cannot describe both. Implemented: data.plugin = the first checked runtime (Claude before Codex), plus an additive data.plugins keyed by runtime (same shape as init's). quest's agents --check checks exactly one target per call, so there is no parity source for the two-runtime case. (B) Only --check detects; a bare or --force lore agents does not, since the --force update is LCLI-593. (C) Ruling 19 says init/--check print the update command for an installed plugin; quest puts it in remedy for installed, and so does this. No ADR-vs-quest-cli discrepancy found in the parts implemented here.

AMENDED (PR #291, new commits, no force-push; merged origin/dev c956cca6 first, clean). (A) Ruling 27, opum-doc ADR Amendment 5, main 99e8ce5, read by ref: lore agents (no --target) now reports plugin state ONLY as data.plugins.<runtime>; the bare data.plugin is removed from AgentsResult, tests assert its absence even with one runtime checked, docs (cli-surface, cli-contract, instructions.ts agents topic) updated. --target not added (LCLI-593, PR #292). lore init unchanged. (B) Review fixes on 194a25ca: 1 HIGH, the runner now spawns detached and SIGKILLs the process group and cancels both pipe readers on the deadline (measured bun 1.3.14: baseline exit 8s after a 1s deadline; cancel alone or group kill alone exit at ~1s; only the group kill reaps the grandchild), plus LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS_TIMEOUT_MS override (LORE_QUEST_TIMEOUT_MS precedent) so a subprocess test can measure lore's own exit; the wrong unref() comment is replaced. 2 MED, reason built with errors.ts stderrHint and every runtime-supplied field (reason, version, scope) reduced to one printable line in core; --scope is only interpolated for a plain token. 3 MED, cli-contract states the host-read exception and LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS=off for determinism, and says the list is not exhaustive (init trackerEnvironment also reads PATH). 4 LOW-MED, same-scope tie broken by deeper projectPath. 5 LOW, /x/foo vs /x/foobar separator test with positive control. 7 LOW, output capped at 1 MiB, past it not-detectable.

AMENDMENT EVIDENCE, lore from source, bun 1.3.14. Gates: full bun test exit 0 (3539 pass, 0 fail, 3540 ran, 110 files); bun run lore check exit 0 (82 files, 0 errors); tsc 0; biome 0. Mutations, each predicted before running: M1 finding 1 reverted (no detached, no group kill, no reader cancel): 1 red, the process-exit test, lore exited at 12192ms, 51 green including the older list()-returns-at-deadline test, which times list() rather than the process. M1b reader cancel restored and group kill still off: same test red on the grandchild-still-alive assertion only, exit at 778ms, so the group kill is pinned separately. M2 finding 2 reverted in both layers: exactly the 3 sanitization cases red, 49 green. M5 separator dropped: exactly the separator case red. M4 depth tie-break dropped: exactly the within-scope ordering case red. All reverted and byte-compared to the fixed files before the gates. Live read-only lore agents --check here: no plugin key, plugins.claude installed 0.9.0 user, exit 0.

FOLLOW-UP, not done here (review finding 6): add LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS=off to the env of ci.yml's 'lore agents --check (bridge currency)' step (bun run lore agents --check), so that CI gate never depends on which agent runtimes a runner has installed. Not changed in this PR because .github/workflows/ci.yml is held by another agent. Today, on a runner with no claude/codex, detection fails fast with ENOENT and reads not-detectable, and the exit code is unaffected either way, so it is a determinism and hygiene fix, not a red gate.

AC2 WORDING vs RULING 27: AC2 reads 'lore agents --check reports data.plugin'. ADR Amendment 5 ruling 27 (opum-doc main 99e8ce5) now forbids a bare data.plugin on a lore agents call with no --target, so the implementation reports data.plugins.<runtime> and asserts data.plugin is absent. AC2 stays checked against the ruling-conforming shape, with that evidence. The criterion's text should be amended to 'data.plugins.<runtime>' by whoever owns the record; this agent did not rewrite an acceptance criterion.
